why: The preset is accepted, applied and published, and what reaches storage is always the shipped default -- so the choice survives exactly as long as the tab does. Issue #540's first acceptance criterion is that it survives a RELOAD, and this is the way to fail it that leaves the whole feature looking correct in a session: the toggle moves, the store notifies, the next match honours it, and the player finds `High` again the following day. Written as the default rather than as a dropped field because a dropped field is the same bug wearing a shape the parser silently repairs.
killedBy: createPlayerSettingsStore: defaults and persistence round-trips EVERY field through a fresh construction
parseSettingsPayload: stored data round-trips its own serialiser exactly
